theory ND

Natural deduction

Depth-indexed object logic, formula validity under all valuations, and soundness of natural deduction.

A depth-indexed object logic and the soundness of natural deduction.

Formulas are indexed by a depth `n`, as `Statement(n)` is in the denotational example (Constable et al. §11.6): `Fml(0)` is empty, and `Fml(n+1)` may mention subformulas of depth `n`. Atoms, conjunction, implication, disjunction, and negation are constructors. A valuation `v : Atom → U{i}` interprets an object formula as a type; each ND rule is a combinator on those types, establishing soundness. Formula validity `Valid2` quantifies over all valuations.

19 theorems, 7 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any piece of syntax for its kind, surface form, and uniform term; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

-- | A depth-indexed object logic and the soundness of natural deduction.
--
-- Formulas are indexed by a depth `n`, as `Statement(n)` is in the
-- denotational example (Constable et al. §11.6): `Fml(0)` is empty, and
-- `Fml(n+1)` may mention subformulas of depth `n`. Atoms, conjunction,
-- implication, disjunction, and negation are constructors.
-- A valuation `v : Atom → U{i}` interprets an object formula as a type;
-- each ND rule is a combinator on those types, establishing soundness.
-- Formula validity `Valid2` quantifies over all valuations.
theory ND

comment book "Depth-indexed object syntax and natural deduction soundness, Constable et al. §11.6."

abs Fst(p) == let <u, v> = p in u
abs Snd(p) == let <u, v> = p in v

-- Fml(n+1) = Atom ⊎ (T × T) ⊎ (T × T) ⊎ T
--   inl a              atom a
--   inr (inl <A,B>)    A ∧ B
--   inr (inr (inl <A,B>))  A → B
--   inr (inr (inr A))  ¬A
abs Fml(n) ==
  ind(n; x,T. Void; Void; x,T. Atom ⊎ ((T × T) ⊎ ((T × T) ⊎ T)))

-- Interpretations at depth 1 (atoms) and depth 2 (one connective)
abs Inter1(v; f) ==
  decide f of
    inl a => v a
  | inr r => False

abs Inter2(v; f) ==
  decide f of
    inl a => v a
  | inr r =>
      decide r of
        inl p => Inter1(v; Fst(p)) ∧ Inter1(v; Snd(p))
      | inr s =>
          decide s of
            inl p => Inter1(v; Fst(p)) → Inter1(v; Snd(p))
          | inr n => ¬(Inter1(v; n))

-- Validity: truth under all atom valuations
abs Valid2(f) == ∀v:(Atom → U{i}). Inter2(v; f)

-- Canonical valuation sending every atom to True
abs Vtrue == λa. True

soft Fst, Snd, Fml, Inter1, Inter2, Valid2, Vtrue

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Formula depth properties
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem fml0_empty :
  Fml(0) = Void ∈ U{i}
proof
  eq
qed

theorem atom_is_fml1 :
  inl "P" ∈ Fml(1)
proof
  auto
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Valuations and interpretations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem inter1_atom :
  ∀v:(Atom → U{i}). ∀a:Atom. Inter1(v; inl a) = v a ∈ U{i}
proof
  intro v
  intro a
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem inter1_P_true :
  Inter1(Vtrue; inl "P")
proof
  reduce
  intro
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Soundness of ND inference rules (on interpreted types)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Hypothesis / assumption: an assumption realizes itself.
theorem nd_hyp :
  ∀A:U{i}. A → A
proof
  intro A
  intro x
  hyp
qed

-- ∧-introduction and eliminations
theorem nd_and_i :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. A → B → A ∧ B
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro a
  intro b
  split THENL [hyp 3, hyp 4]
qed

theorem nd_and_e1 :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. A ∧ B → A
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro p
  elim 3
  hyp
qed

theorem nd_and_e2 :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. A ∧ B → B
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro p
  elim 3
  hyp
qed

-- ∨-introductions and elimination (case analysis)
theorem nd_or_i1 :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. A → A ∨ B
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro a
  left
  hyp
qed

theorem nd_or_i2 :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. B → A ∨ B
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro b
  right
  hyp
qed

theorem nd_or_e :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀C:U{i}. (A ∨ B) → (A → C) → (B → C) → C
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro C
  intro ab
  intro ac
  intro bc
  elim 4 THENL [
    elim 5 with u THENL [hyp, hyp],
    elim 6 with v THENL [hyp, hyp]
  ]
qed

-- →-introduction and elimination (modus ponens)
theorem nd_imp_i :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. (A → B) → (A → B)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro f
  hyp
qed

theorem nd_imp_e :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. (A → B) → A → B
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro f
  intro x
  elim 3 with x THENL [hyp, hyp]
qed

-- ¬-introduction and explosion (ex falso quodlibet)
theorem nd_not_i :
  ∀A:U{i}. (A → False) → ¬A
proof
  intro A
  intro f
  hyp
qed

theorem nd_false_e :
  ∀A:U{i}. False → A
proof
  intro A
  intro p
  elim 2
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Soundness of object-level connectives at depth 2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem and_intro_sound :
  ∀v:(Atom → U{i}). ∀a:Atom. ∀b:Atom.
    Inter1(v; inl a) → Inter1(v; inl b) →
    Inter2(v; inr (inl (<inl a, inl b>)))
proof
  intro v
  intro a
  intro b
  intro pa
  intro pb
  reduce
  split THENL [hyp 4, hyp 5]
qed

theorem imp_intro_sound :
  ∀v:(Atom → U{i}). ∀a:Atom. ∀b:Atom.
    (Inter1(v; inl a) → Inter1(v; inl b)) →
    Inter2(v; inr (inr (inl (<inl a, inl b>))))
proof
  intro v
  intro a
  intro b
  intro f
  reduce
  hyp
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Validity of object logic tautologies
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- For any atom `a`, the implication `a → a` is valid across all valuations.
theorem valid_id :
  ∀a:Atom. Valid2(inr (inr (inl (<inl a, inl a>))))
proof
  intro a
  intro v
  reduce
  intro x
  hyp
qed

-- Exemplary ND derivation of `P → P` at depth 2 under `Vtrue`.
theorem identity_derivation :
  Inter2(Vtrue; inr (inr (inl (<inl "P", inl "P">))))
proof
  reduce
  intro x
  hyp
qed
